source_text:
καταστή σειεν ἕξιν, γοερῷ τινι καὶ πολυθρηνώδει παραδοὺς αὐτὸν βίῳ· τὸν δὲ καὶ
πρὸ τού των φεύγοντα μὲν κώμους, διώκοντα δὲ ἀν θρώπους παίζοντας καὶ
γελωτοποιοῦντας, ποῖον ἂν ἔχοι λόγον ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς σκύθρωπον καὶ κατηφῆ βίον;
ἐπειδὴ κατεσκληκὼς ἤμην καὶ κατεστυμμένος, οὐκ ἐπὶ τὰς διαφορού σας ἐκείνῳ τῷ
βίῳ κακίας κατέπεσα. 380 λαʹ. Εἰ δὲ καὶ πολλάκις εἶπον αἱ θερά παιναί μου· Τίς ἂν
δῴη ἡμῖν τῶν σαρκῶν αὐτοῦ πλησθῆναι, λίαν μου χρηστοῦ ὄντος; Ἀντὶ τῆς ζωῆς
αὐτοῦ ἀπολαῦσαι, ὅτι ἤμην αὐταῖς γλυκύς. λβʹ. Ἔξω δὲ οὐκ ηὐλίζετο ξένος, ἡ δὲ
θύρα μου παντὶ ἐλθόντι ἠνέῳκτο. Οὐ γὰρ ἐθεράπευεν αὐτοὺς ὑποδεχόμενος μόνον,
ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐφόδια τῆς μετὰ ταῦτα πενίας παρεῖχεν. Κεφ. ΛΒʹ, αʹ. Καὶ ἐπαύσατο Ἰὼβ
ῥήμα σιν. Ἡσύχασεν μὲν ὁ Ἰὼβ, διδοὺς αὐτοῖς λό γον εἰπεῖν· ἐνεῖδε δὲ, καὶ τὸν Θεὸν
ἐκάλεσε μάρτυρα, καὶ ἑαυτῷ ἐπηράσατο ὅτι ἐπεστο μίσθησαν οἱ φίλοι. ιαʹ. Ἐρῶ γὰρ,
ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων, ἄχρις οὗ ἐτάσητε λόγους, καὶ μέχρι ὑμῶν συνήσω. Ἢ τοῦτό
φησιν, ὅτι οὐδὲ ὅτε ἠλέγχετε, ὡς ἔδει, ἠλέγξατε· ἢ ὅτι ὕστερον ἐσιωπή σατε. Οὕτω
πρὸς τό· Ἐρῶ γὰρ, ὑμῶν ἀκου όντων. Κεφ. ΛΓʹ, ιβʹ. Πῶς γὰρ λέγεις· ∆ίκαιός εἰμι, καὶ
οὐκ ἐπακήκοέ μου; Τί οὖν ἐγένετο; οὐχὶ τοῦτο ἐνόμιζεν· τοῦτο μὲν γὰρ ὑπελάμβανεν
ὁ Ἐλιοὺς, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ τοιαύτῃ γνώμῃ ὁ Ἰὼβ εἶπεν, ὅτι οὗτος δικαιότερός ἐστι τοῦ
Θεοῦ· ἀλλ' ὅτι ταῦτα μὲν αὐτῷ πέπρακται, οὐ μὴν ἀδικίαν ἐνεκά λει τῷ Θεῷ. Ὁ δὲ
Ἐλιοὺς τοῦτο ὑπέλαβεν· ἐκείνοις δὲ δικαίως ἐνεκάλει, προσδεδωκόσι τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸ
μέρος καὶ ἠρνημένοις. 381 κʹ. Λαλήσω, ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι ἀνοίξας τὰ χείλη. Ὁ
τυγχάνων συνετοῦ ἀκροατοῦ, καὶ ὢν πλήρης λόγων, λαλῶν ἀναπαύεται, τὴν πε
ριττότητα οἷον κενώσας καὶ ἀποβάλλων, καὶ λέγει· Λαλήσω ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι. Κεφ.
Λ∆ʹ, ιθʹ. Ὃς οὐκ ἐπαισχυνθῇ πρόσω πον ἐντίμου, οὐδὲ οἶδε τιμὴν θέσθαι ἁδροῖς. Εἰ
γὰρ καὶ μὴ οἶδας, ἀλλ' ὀφείλεις πολλὰ παραχωρεῖν αὐτῷ, καὶ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ, ὥστε
μὴ πάντα ζητεῖν μανθάνειν. κγʹ. Ὅτι οὐκ ἐπ' ἄνδρα θήσει ἔτι. Ἔοικε τοῦτο λέγειν,
ὅτι νῦν μὲν ἐν ἡμῖν κεῖται τὸ καλὸν καὶ τὸ φαῦλον, ἐν δὲ τῷ μέλλοντι αἰῶνι οὐκ ἔτι.
λαʹ. Ὅτι πρὸς τὸν ἰσχυρὸν ὁ λέγων· Εἴ ληφα, οὐκ ἐνεχυράσω, ἄνευ ἐμαυτοῦ ὄψομαι·
σὺ δεῖξόν μοι. Τινὲς οὕτως ἡρμήνευσαν· ὅτι μὴ τολμᾷ τις εἰπεῖν τῷ ἰσχυρωτέρῳ, ὅτι
ἀδίκως εἴ ληφας τὰ ἐμὰ, οὐκ ἐνεχύρου χάριν, ὡς ὑπο φειλόμενα, καὶ παρὰ γνώμην
ἐμὴν εἴληφας· ἐπίδειξον ὅτι εὐλόγως τοῦτο δέδρακας. Εἰ δὲ τῷ δυνατῷ ταῦτα οὐδεὶς
εἰπεῖν τολμᾷ, πῶς σὺ, φησὶ, τοιαῦτα θρασύνῃ κατὰ Θεόν; Ὁ δὲ Σύμμαχος οὕτως
ἐκδέδωκεν, ὅτι πρὸς Θεὸν ῥῆσιν ἀνέλαβον, οὐχ ἕξω ἀκω 382 λύτως, σὺ διασάφησόν
μοι. Ὁ δὲ ἐνόησεν οὕτως, τουτέστιν· ἐπειδὴ τὴν ὑπὲρ Θεοῦ ῥῆσιν ἀνέλαβον, φησὶν
Ἐλιοὺς, οὐκ ἐπέχω, ἀλλ' ἀκωλύτως ἐπεξέρχομαι τῷ λόγῳ. Εἰ δὲ μὴ καλῶς λέγω, σὺ
διασάφησον, ἀντὶ τοῦ, ἔλεγξον τὸν λόγον. –Οἶμαι δὲ μᾶλ λον οὕτω νοεῖσθαι τὸ
κείμενον, ὅτι οὐκ ἐπειδὴ τὸ ὑπὲρ Θεοῦ λέγειν εἱλόμην, παρὰ τοῦτο δεῖ σε καὶ
συνομολογεῖν ἁπλῶς, οἷα δὴ χρέος ἀπαιτῶ· ἄνευ δὲ ἐμαυτοῦ ὄψομαι, σὺ δεῖξόν μοι,
ἀντὶ τοῦ· χωρὶς τοῦ ἐμοῦ λόγου εἰδέναι θέλω, εἴ τι καὶ ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοις· ἵνα εἴπῃς ὅτι
ἡσυχίαν παρέχομαι, καὶ ἐπιλαμβάνου τὸν λόγον, εἰ δύνασαι. Κεφ. ΛΕʹ, εʹ. Ἀνάβλεψον
εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν. Οὐδεὶς φιλόκοσμος ἀναβλέπει εἰς τὸν οὐ ρανόν· μὴ ἀγαπῶμεν τὸν
κόσμον, μηδὲ τὰ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ. Εἰ τὰ ἐνθένδε ἀγαπῶμεν, οὐκ ἀναβλέπομεν εἰς τὸν
οὐρανόν. ʹ. Εἰ ἥμαρτες, τί πράξεις; Τουτέστιν οὐδὲ αὐτὸν ἀδικήσεις, ἀλλ' οὐ δὲ
ὠφελήσεις, δίκαιος ὤν· ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἔλε γεν· Εἰ ἥμαρτον, τί δύναμαι πρᾶξαι; τί
ποιήσω, φησίν; τοῦτο ἵνα εἴπῃ· ∆ιὰ τί; μὴ γὰρ ἀδικούμενος φροντίζει σου ἁμαρτάνον
τος; μὴ γὰρ ὡς βλάβην ὑπομένων; ιʹ. Ὁ κατατάσσων φυλακὰς νυκτερινάς. Θέλεις
ἰδεῖν πῶς κατατάσσει φυλακὰς νυκτερινὰς ὁ Θεός; ὅλος ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος νύξ ἐστι,
σκότος ἐστί. Τὸ φῶς τηρεῖταί σοι· ὃ βλέπεις νῦν φῶς, δι' ἔσοπτρον βλέπεις. Καί· Ἐν
τῷ φωτί σου ὀψόμεθα φῶς· μέλλομεν ποτὲ βλέπειν αὐτό. Οὐκοῦν νύξ ἐστι πᾶς ὁ
αἰών; ἐπεὶ νύξ ἐστι, πολέμιοι πολλοὶ, πολλὰ θηρία περιέρχονται. Ἐπεὶ οὖν νύξ ἐστὶ
τὰ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ τοῦ βίου πράγματα, χρεία ἐστι φυ λάκων τεταγμένων εἰς τὴν νύκτα
ταύτην, 383 ἵνα οἱ φύλακες, οἱ ἐπὶ τῶν νυκτῶν, φρουρῶσι τοὺς ἐν νυκτὶ, καὶ ἔλθωσι
καὶ φυλάξωσιν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν λῃστῶν. Τίνες οὖν οἱ φύλα κες, οἱ τεταγμένοι παρὰ
τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς φυλακαῖς ταῖς νυκτεριναῖς; Παρεμβαλεῖ ἄγ γελος Κυρίου κύκλῳ
τῶν φοβουμένων αὐτὸν, καὶ ῥύσεται αὐτούς· οὗτοι οἱ ἄγγελοι οἳ ἐν νυκτὶ
pass_a_gloss: [continuing from the previous section: 'for the laughter-lover ... fittingly setting against, the contrary'] state he would establish, handing him over to a wailing and much-lamenting life; but the one who even before these things fled revels and chased (drove off) men playing and making laughter, what reason would he have to fall into a sullen and downcast life? since I was dried up (withered) and austere, I did not fall upon the vices belonging (διαφορούσας read διαφερούσας) to that life. Verse 31. And if also often my maidservants said: Who would give us to be filled of his flesh, I being very kind? Instead of (that is): to enjoy his life, because I was sweet to them. Verse 32. Outside a stranger did not lodge, and my door was opened to everyone who came. For he did not only serve them by receiving, but also provided supplies (travel provisions) for the poverty after these things. Chapter 32, verse 1. And Job ceased from words. Job was quiet, giving them word (room) to speak; but he looked in (noticed), and called God witness, and cursed himself, because (that) the friends were muzzled. Verse 11. For I will speak, you listening, until you examine words, and as far as you I will understand (attend). Either he says this, that not even when you refuted, did you refute as was needed; or that later you fell silent. Thus toward the [words]: For I will speak, you listening. Chapter 33, verse 12. For how do you say: I am just, and he did not hear me? What then happened? He did not think this; for this Elihu supposed, but not with such a mind did Job speak, that this man is more just than God; but that these things were done by him, yet he did not charge injustice against God. But Elihu supposed this; and those he justly charged, having betrayed (προσδεδωκόσι read προδεδωκόσι) the part of God and having denied. Verse 20. I will speak, so that I may rest, having opened the lips. The one meeting an intelligent hearer, and being full of words, speaking rests, as it were emptying and throwing off the superfluity, and says: I will speak so that I may rest. Chapter 34, verse 19. Who would not be ashamed before the face of an honoured one, nor knows to set honour to the stout (great). For even if you do not know, yet you owe to concede many things to him, and to his glory, so as not to seek to learn all things. Verse 23. For not upon a man will he set any longer. He seems to say this, that now in us lies the good and the bad, but in the coming age no longer. Verse 31. For toward the strong one the one saying: I have taken, I will not take pledge, without myself I will see; you show me. Some interpreted thus: that no one dares say to the stronger, that unjustly you took my things, not for the sake of a pledge, as owed, and against my mind you took; show that reasonably you did this. But if to the powerful no one dares say these things, how do you, he says, grow bold in such things against God? Symmachus rendered thus: that toward God I took up speech, I will not hold, unhinderedly, you make clear to me. And he understood thus, that is: since I took up the speech on behalf of God, says Elihu, I do not hold back, but unhinderedly I go on with the word. If I do not speak well, you make clear, instead of (that is), refute the word. I think rather thus the text is understood, that not since I chose to speak on behalf of God, by this you must also agree simply, as indeed I demand a debt; but without myself I will see, you show me, instead of: apart from my word I want to know, if you have anything to say against; that you may speak, I furnish quiet, and take hold of the word, if you can. Chapter 35, verse 5. Look up into heaven. No world-lover looks up into heaven; let us not love the world, nor the things in the world. If we love the things from here, we do not look up into heaven. Verse 6 (numeral lost in OCR). If you sinned, what will you do? That is, neither will you wrong him, but neither will you help, being just; for since he was saying: If I sinned, what can I do? what will I do, he says; this so that he may say: Why? for being wronged does he care about you sinning? as enduring harm? Verse 10. The one appointing night watches. Do you want to see how God appoints night watches? this whole age is night, is darkness. The light is kept for you; what light you see now, you see through a mirror. And: In your light we will see light; we are going some time to see it. So is not the whole age night? since it is night, enemies many, many beasts go about. Since then the affairs in the darkness of life are night, there is need of guards stationed for this night, so that the guards, those over the nights, may guard those in night, and may come and guard us from the robbers. Who then are the guards stationed by God in the night watches? An angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him, and will rescue them; these the angels who in night [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … condition he would bring about, handing him over to a mournful life of many laments. But the one who even before these things shunned revels and drove off people who joke and play the clown, what reason could there be for him to fall into a sullen and downcast life? Since I was already withered and austere, I did not fall into the vices that belong to that life.
“And if my maidservants often said, ‘Who would grant us to be filled with his flesh?’, for I was very kind” (Job 31:31). That is, to enjoy his life, because I was sweet to them.

“No stranger lodged outside, and my door was open to everyone who came” (Job 31:32). For he did not only care for them by taking them in, but also supplied them with provisions against the poverty that would follow.
“And Job ceased from words” (Job 31:40). Job fell silent, giving them room to speak; but he took note, called God as witness and called down curses on himself, because his friends had been silenced.

“For I will speak while you listen, until you have examined the words, and I will attend to you” (Job 32:11-12). Either he is saying this: even when you were refuting, you did not refute as you should have; or that afterwards you fell silent. That is how it bears on “For I will speak while you listen.”

“For how do you say, ‘I am righteous, and he has not heard me’?” (Job 33:12). What then happened? He did not think this. Elihu supposed it, but Job did not speak with any such mind, that he was more righteous than God; he meant that he had done these things, and yet he did not charge God with injustice. Elihu supposed this. But he rightly charged those others, who had betrayed God's side and denied it.

“I will speak, that I may rest, when I have opened my lips” (Job 32:20). One who has found an intelligent hearer and is full of words finds rest in speaking, as though emptying out and casting off the excess; and he says, “I will speak, that I may rest.”

“He who did not feel shame before the face of one held in honour, nor knows how to pay honour to the great” (Job 34:19). For even if you do not know, you still ought to yield much to him and to his glory, so as not to seek to learn everything.
“For he will no longer lay it upon a man” (Job 34:23). He seems to be saying this: now the good and the bad lie with us, but in the age to come no longer.

“For as for the one who says to the Mighty One, ‘I have received; I will not take a pledge; apart from myself I shall see; you show me’” (Job 34:31-32). Some have interpreted it thus: no one dares to say to one who is stronger, “You have taken what is mine unjustly, not by way of a pledge, as though it were owed to you, and you have taken it against my will; show that you have done this with good reason.” But if no one dares to say these things to a man of power, how, he says, can you be so bold as to say such things against God?

Symmachus rendered it thus: “Since I have taken up speech towards God, I will not hold back; unhindered, you make it plain to me.” His meaning is this: since I have taken up speech on God's behalf, says Elihu, I do not hold back, but go on with the argument unhindered. And if I do not speak well, you make it plain, that is, refute the argument.

But I think rather that the text should be understood thus: it is not that, because I have chosen to speak on God's behalf, you must for that reason simply agree with me as well, as though I were demanding payment of a debt. “Apart from myself I shall see; you show me” means: apart from my own argument I want to know whether you have anything to say in reply. I keep silence so that you may speak; take up the argument, if you can.

“Look up to heaven” (Job 35:5). No lover of the world looks up to heaven. Let us not love the world, nor the things in the world (1 John 2:15). If we love the things here, we do not look up to heaven.

“If you have sinned, what will you do?” (Job 35:6). That is, you will not wrong him; but neither will you benefit him if you are righteous. For since he was saying, “If I have sinned, what can I do?” (Job 7:20), “What shall I do?” he says, this is in order to say: Why? Does he care about your sinning because he is wronged? As though he suffered harm?

“He who appoints night watches” (Job 35:10). Do you want to see how God appoints night watches? This whole age is night; it is darkness. The light is kept for you: the light you see now, you see through a mirror (1 Corinthians 13:12). And: “In your light we shall see light” (Psalm 36:9); one day we are to see it. Is not the whole age, then, night? Since it is night, there are many enemies; many wild beasts prowl about. Since, then, the affairs in the darkness of this life are night, there is need of guards posted for this night, so that the guards, those set over the nights, may keep watch over those who are in the night, and may come and guard us from the robbers. Who, then, are the guards posted by God in the night watches? “The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him, and will deliver them” (Psalm 34:7). These are the angels who in the night …

choices.choice: Old English was a garbled near-transliteration with stray OCR ('F my sorrowful women', 'Lb.', '381 k.', 'X.') and wrong catena labels ('Ch. 24, 1', 'Ch. 25, 12', 'Ch. 26, 18', 'Ch. 45, 5'). Retranslated clause by clause; each lemma opens a paragraph with its verse.

'pursuing men who play and make merry' replaced: διώκοντα here means driving them off, in contrast to the luxury-lover. 'The one who is a thoughtful listener' replaced: ὁ τυγχάνων συνετοῦ ἀκροατοῦ = one who has found an intelligent hearer. 'nor knows how to grant honor to the simple' replaced: ἁδροῖς = the great. 'so as not to seek all things, but to learn' replaced: ὥστε μὴ πάντα ζητεῖν μανθάνειν = so as not to seek to learn everything. 'we undertook an oath toward God' replaced: ῥῆσιν = speech. 'declaring that his friends had ceased to accuse' replaced: ἐπεστομίσθησαν = had been silenced.

Old 'the Ally explained' was Ὁ δὲ Σύμμαχος misread; now 'Symmachus rendered it thus'. The punctuation of Symmachus' text (οὐχ ἕξω ἀκωλύτως, σὺ διασάφησόν μοι) is uncertain; rendered 'I will not hold back; unhindered, you make it plain to me', and the next sentence ('His meaning is this') gives the paraphrase the catena offers.
καταστήσειεν ἕξιν completes 'τὴν ἐναντίαν' at the end of u02-rem-early ('he fittingly sets the opposite …'); rendered '… condition he would bring about'.

διαφορούσας read διαφερούσας ('that belong to'); προσδεδωκόσι read προδεδωκόσι ('betrayed'); the stigma numeral before Εἰ ἥμαρτες is lost ('ʹ') and restored as ϛʹ = 35:6; page numbers 380-383 dropped.

choices.issue: Ἀντὶ τῆς ζωῆς αὐτοῦ ἀπολαῦσαι (31:31 note)
choices.choice: Taken as the catena's Ἀντὶ τοῦ formula ('that is'), as the morning log renders it: 'That is, to enjoy his life'.

Ambiguous: ὅτι may depend on ἐνεῖδε ('he saw that the friends were silenced') or give the reason. Rendered 'he took note, called God as witness and called down curses on himself, because his friends had been silenced'; a human may prefer 'he saw that'.

Κεφ. ΛΒʹ αʹ heads 'And Job ceased from words', which is LXX and KJV 31:40 (KJV: 'The words of Job are ended'), not 32:1; cited Job 31:40. The κʹ lemma after the 33:12 note is LXX 32:20 ('I will speak, that I may rest'), printed out of order in the catena; cited Job 32:20.
ἐκείνοις δὲ δικαίως ἐνεκάλει: 'he rightly charged those others' kept with an unnamed subject (Elihu in context, cf. Job 32:3), as the Greek does not name him.
